item.title: #3592001: Apply page variant translation overrides to previews
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592001 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

In Drupal Canvas, when a PageVariant (or a page region) has a config translation, the translated text never showed up in the editor's own preview of that variant, and it also failed to show up in the page chrome wrapped around content previews whenever the page variant had an unsaved auto-save draft. Switching the language dropdown in the editor, or opening a preview URL with a language parameter, kept showing the original base-language text even though the live front end correctly rendered the translation. This made the editor's language switcher effectively non-functional on those two preview surfaces. The fix makes both preview paths apply the language's translation override before rendering, so what editors see in preview now matches what visitors actually see on the live site.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Canvas intentionally keeps its client model and PATCH operations on untranslated base config; translation is meant to surface only at preview/render time, driven by the requested preview language. Two rendering paths were missing that step. ApiLayoutController::buildPreviewRenderable() built the preview straight from the upcast base entity's component tree via componentTreeLoader, never consulting any LanguageConfigOverride. CanvasPageVariant::buildPageVariant(), when a valid auto-save draft exists, renders that draft's tree, but drafts live in key/value storage outside the config system, so a LanguageConfigOverride structurally cannot apply to them, leaving the chrome permanently base-language whenever a draft was present.

Both fixes reuse the existing ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::getTranslatedComponentTree(), which merges the base tree (including a draft's tree) with a language's override. In ApiLayoutController, the current interface language (from the newly injected LanguageManagerInterface) is checked against $entity->getTranslationLanguages(include_default: FALSE); if it has a stored override, the merged tree is used instead of the raw one, and the render array gets a languages:interface cache context added (no separate cache tag is needed since the override shares the base config's cache tag). CanvasPageVariant gets a new private getPreviewComponentTree() helper that does the same check and is used by both buildPageVariant() and the legacy-regions rendering path, but only when $is_preview is true; live (non-preview) rendering is untouched. LanguageManagerInterface was added to the plugin's constructor via create().</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3592000: Translating a component tree config entity (such as PageVariant) that has an auto-save draft breaks Canvas layout validation
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592000 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

If a PageVariant or ContentTemplate had unpublished changes sitting in Canvas's auto-save draft when it was translated via config translation, the next time anyone opened the Canvas editor it would crash with a 500 error on every layout request, and stay crashed since the error masked the whole screen (there was no way to publish or discard the draft to recover). This affected plain, single-language-default sites, not just multilingual ones with langcode drift. The fix stops this crash: translating an entity that has a pending auto-save draft no longer breaks the editor.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The crash came from CanvasConfigEntityTranslationsAreValidConstraintValidator::validate(), which simulates Config::setOverriddenData() by running NestedArray::mergeDeepArray() on the entity's base component_tree and the LanguageConfigOverride's translated data, then validates the merged array against config schema. A saved component_tree is re-keyed by instance UUID in ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::preSave(), but an auto-save draft never runs preSave(), so a draft created before the translation existed keeps the client's delta keys (0, 1, 2, …). A LanguageConfigOverride, however, always targets instances by UUID. Merging a delta-keyed base with a UUID-keyed override made the merge treat them as disjoint sets, appending the override's sparse translated inputs as a phantom component instance with no component_id, component_version, or uuid. Validating that merged data tripped the assert(\array_key_exists('component_id', $component_instance)) in ComponentInputsMapping::__construct().

The fix re-keys the base component_tree by UUID before the merge, calling ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::asDeterministicallyAndTranslatableKeyedComponentTreeSequence(), mirroring what getTranslatedComponentTree() already did for a different code path (as noted in that method's own docblock). Test coverage was added in PageVariantValidationTest::testValidationWithTranslationOverrideAndDeltaKeyedTree, which reconstructs the delta-keyed draft shape, adds a UUID-targeted hu override, and asserts no validation errors. This fix was split out of the broader langcode-drift work in #3591850 (MR !1400) because it reproduces under plain, single-language-default conditions.

Upgrade

No action needed for typical Canvas usage; this is an internal bug fix. For context: ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::asDeterministicallyAndTranslatableKeyedComponentTreeSequence() was changed from private to public (and marked @internal) so the validator could reuse the same re-keying logic. It remains an internal method not intended for use outside Canvas core.

item.title: #3591981: Provide consistent Code Component metadata validation across CLI and Drupal
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591981 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas Code Components are described by an authored component.yml file, but until now the rules for what counts as valid metadata were scattered across the CLI, JSON Schema prop definitions, Drupal config schema, and PHP entity constraints. That made local feedback incomplete and meant errors could surface only partway through a canvas push, after other components had already been updated. This change publishes a single, hand-authored JSON Schema for the authored component.yml envelope and adds a Drupal endpoint that authoritatively validates a component's metadata against the target site without saving it. The Canvas CLI now runs local structural and ESLint checks first, then calls the target site to confirm acceptance, and canvas push preflights every component's metadata before making any changes so a rejected component no longer leaves a push partially applied. Sites without the new endpoint fall back to the previous per-component, save-time validation.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New authenticated, non-mutating POST /canvas/api/v0/code-components/validate endpoint runs the same entity and metadata constraint chain as create/update and returns 204 or structured constraint violations without saving anything.

Technical details

The envelope contract lives in the repository-root component-metadata.schema.json (draft-07, published at the 1.x rolling raw URL), requiring only name and machineName and rejecting unknown keys and projected x-allowed-* keys; it is statically bundled into the CLI rather than fetched at runtime, and prop definitions under props.properties are validated directly as JSON Schema (including their first example) rather than generated from Drupal's config schema. A new private packages/json-schema-validation workspace package (createCanvasAjv) centralizes a strict draft-07 Ajv instance with ajv-formats and ajv-formats-draft2019, shared by the UI and CLI, replacing the UI's local ui/src/utils/ajv.ts.

On the Drupal side, ApiCodeComponentMetadataController::validatePayload (route canvas.api.code_component.validate, permission administer code components) builds an in-memory JavaScriptComponent create or update candidate from the posted payload and runs getTypedData()->validate(), returning 204 on success or throwing a ConstraintViolationException with the structured violations otherwise; unresolvable json-schema-definitions:// references are converted into a violation instead of a fatal error. In packages/cli, validate.ts and push.ts (via new utils/target-component-metadata.ts and services/api.ts additions) submit each component's normalized payload to this endpoint when an authenticated API service is available, and canvas push now calls preflightCodeComponentPayloads() before any create, update, or delete, aborting the push with "Nothing was pushed" if any component fails. When the target endpoint or authentication is unavailable, the CLI emits a warning that only local checks ran and continues, and older sites without the route retain the previous partial, per-save validation. The old duplicate validators validate-content-entity-reference.ts and ESLint rules component-content-entity-reference-props and component-prop-example-value-image-url were removed in favor of the Drupal-side authoritative checks plus a new, more general component-required-props ESLint rule.

item.title: #3591972: Code editor has no "Document" prop type for the document object shape
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591972 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

Canvas's code editor previously recognized only "Image" and "Video" object prop types. A code component prop using the newly added document schema shape ($ref to canvas.module/document) would silently vanish from the Props panel, and there was no way to add a new document prop from the UI. This fix adds full "Document" prop type support: it appears in the prop type selector, has its own configuration form, supports single and multi-value (allow multiple) modes, and shows a filename/file-type chip instead of a broken image preview when a document is set as a prop's default value.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Code components can declare a prop with $ref: json-schema-definitions://canvas.module/document, exposed in the code editor as a "Document" prop type.

Technical details

The root cause was that derivedPropTypes.ts had no entry mapping the document $ref to a prop type, so Props.tsx derived null for such props and filtered them out. The fix adds a document entry (displayName: 'Document') whose derive callback matches $ref === 'json-schema-definitions://canvas.module/document', with an init example carrying src, filename, and mimetype. As part of this, the existing image and video derive callbacks were tightened from $ref?.includes('image')/includes('video') substring checks to exact $ref equality checks, since substring matching became ambiguous with three object $refs in play.

Props.tsx gained a case 'document': branch rendering a new FormPropTypeDocument component, and 'document' was added alongside 'image'/'video' everywhere those two were special-cased: the limited-count array handling, the "has a dedicated example form" check that suppresses the generic required-prop default, the allow-multiple whitelist, and the limited/unlimited valueMode switch. utils.ts's serializeExample/deserialization logic gained an isDocument flag so multi-value document examples get the same empty-src filtering and URL rewriting as image and video examples.

On the PHP side, JsComponent::EXAMPLE_URL_ALLOW_LIST (replacing two separate constant checks) now also allows the new EXAMPLE_DOCUMENT constant (/ui/assets/documents/sample.pdf) as a root-relative example URL for validation purposes. DefaultImagePreview.tsx, which previously rendered a raw <img src> for any media-library-style prop default, now detects document values ('filename' in value || 'mimetype' in value) and renders a file-extension chip with a filename label instead of attempting to render a PDF as an image.</technical> <parameter name="collaboration">

item.title: #3591970: Components library UI is broken if a single component preview rendering fails: treat them as "errored" instead so they cannot be placed but the listing is still functional
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591970 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

In Canvas, if a single component's preview render failed (for example, a Views block whose display requires URL arguments that Canvas cannot supply), the entire Components library UI broke and became unusable, blocking editors from placing any component at all. Now such a component is simply marked as "broken" and excluded from placement, while every other component in the library keeps working normally.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The crash happened in Component::normalizeForClientSide(). Previously, only components already known to be broken via ComponentSourceInterface::isBroken() were wrapped in a try/catch; components that passed that check but then threw during getClientSideInfo() or during RendererInterface::renderInIsolation() were not caught, so an uncaught \Throwable bubbled up and turned the whole ApiConfigControllers::list() response into a 500, taking down the entire library listing.

The fix unifies both code paths (the "known broken" branch and the "renders preview" branch) under a single try/catch (\Throwable $e) block, so any crash during preview building or rendering is now caught and converted into a per-component "broken" state via RenderSafeComponentContainer::handleComponentException(), rather than propagating. EnforcedResponseException and FormAjaxException are explicitly re-thrown rather than swallowed, since those are Drupal Form API flow-control exceptions that must keep bubbling (noted as a workaround pending #2367555). A related @todo references #3521041 for eventually simplifying the RenderSafeComponentContainer wrapping logic itself.

Test coverage was added: CanvasTestBlockInputValidatableCrash gained a static $forceCrash flag so a block can be made to crash unconditionally (mirroring a Views-backed block crashing while building its preview), and BlockComponentTest::testCrashingPreviewDoesNotBreakComponentList() asserts that the crashing component is reported with broken => TRUE and a "Component failed to render" message, while unrelated components in the same listing remain present and broken => FALSE.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3591916: Component version hashes go stale on single-process installs: prop-shape re-resolution is deferred to teardown and skipped on a cold cache
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591916 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Sites built with the Canvas module and installed in a single process (for example via drush site:install applying recipes, as opposed to the browser installer) could end up with Component config entities whose version hash did not match the site's actual configuration. This happened when one recipe created config that changes how a component's properties are stored, such as the first image media type changing how an image prop is saved. If a later recipe in the same install shipped a component tree (a page region, content template, or pattern) referencing the corrected version hash, that hash did not actually exist yet on the freshly installed site, causing a hard render failure. The bug was invisible in bug reports because running drush cr, installing another module, or saving a View or Menu afterward silently fixed the stale hashes. This is now corrected: single-process installs produce the same, correct component version history as the browser installer.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause was in PersistentPropShapeRepository, which caches "storable prop shapes" (how a component prop is actually stored, e.g. as a plain image field vs. a Media Library reference) and computes Component version hashes from them. When a cache tag invalidation queued a prop shape for re-resolution (resolveBeforeWrite), that queue was previously only drained at destruct() (request/process teardown), never before the current process's own component-generation pass read the shapes. Additionally, updateCache() had a cold-cache guard that skipped generateComponents() entirely, which is always true on a fresh install, so the corrected shapes got cached without ever regenerating the Components that depend on them.

The fix adds resolveInvalidatedPropShapes() to PropShapeRepositoryInterface, implemented in PersistentPropShapeRepository to synchronously drain the queued re-resolutions (and a no-op in EphemeralPropShapeRepository, which never caches). This is now called from JsonSchemaPropsComponentDiscoveryBase::getPropsForComponentPlugin(), right before it reads prop shapes to compute prop field definitions and version hashes, so RecipeSubscriber::ensureComponentsExist(), hook_rebuild(), and module-install triggers all see up-to-date shapes. updateCache()'s cold-cache guard was also narrowed: it now only skips regeneration when nothing was actually invalidated during the process (i.e. shapes were merely resolved for the first time), but always regenerates when resolveBeforeWrite was non-empty, even on a cold cache, since that means the storable shapes genuinely changed mid-process.

A related, separate gap, array-item prop shapes not carrying the config:media_type_list cache tag, is tracked separately in #3591917 and was not addressed here.

item.title: #3591885: Add `document` object $ref for linking locally hosted documents
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591885 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Drupal Canvas code components and Single Directory Components (SDCs) can now declare a "document" prop, the same way they already can for image and video. A component that accepts a document (or an array of them) gets a file upload widget for content authors, or the Media Library picker when Media Library is enabled and a compatible media type exists, and receives the document's URL, title, filename, size, and MIME type. This was split off from the broader video/embed proposal in #3524130 because linking a local document has no dependency on the postponed core oEmbed work, unlike remote video.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New document object shape (json-schema-definitions://canvas.module/document) that code components and SDCs can $ref to declare a document/file-download prop with src, title, description, filename, filesize, and mimetype.

Technical details

The new shape is defined in schema.json as document, requiring only src (a uri-reference restricted to http/https via x-allowed-schemes) and adding an x-allowed-file-extensions annotation listing common office and document formats. It is registered as JsonSchemaObjectRef::Document and added to the Choice constraint in config/schema/canvas.json_schema.yml alongside image and video.

Storage matching is handled in JsonSchemaType::computeStorablePropShape(), which maps Document to a file field (fieldWidget: file_generic) with src, filename, filesize, and mimetype resolved from the referenced File entity's uri, filename, filesize, and filemime; the field's file_extensions instance setting is derived from the shape's x-allowed-file-extensions list via the new JsonSchemaObjectRef::allowedFileExtensions(). title and description are left unmapped because a plain file field exposes neither.

To support Media Library, the media-source-to-schema mapping (previously a private array and method inside ShapeMatchingHooks) was extracted into a new internal MediaSourceObjectShapes class shared by both the media library integration and EntityFieldPropSourceMatcher. It maps Document to \Drupal\media\Plugin\media\Source\File, matching any media type whose source is File (but not a more specific subclass like VideoFile) and whose source field's allowed extensions intersect the shape's list; this intersection logic is carried by a new no-op UriTargetFileExtensionsConstraint/validator pair, mirroring how UriTargetMediaTypeConstraint narrows matches by MIME type. EntityFieldPropSourceMatcher gained matchDocumentShapeToMediaTypes() to also suggest existing single-value media reference fields pointing at compatible media types, one reference level deep. Embedding or previewing the document, and remote-video support, remain out of scope, per the split from #3524130 and the still-postponed #3567249.

item.title: #3591968: Forbid the reserved component tree root UUID as a component instance `uuid`/`parent_uuid`
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591968 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Every Canvas component tree has a synthetic root, identified internally by a fixed, reserved UUID. Because that UUID happens to be a syntactically valid v4 UUID, nothing previously stopped a component instance from using it as its own uuid, or from pointing to it as its parent_uuid. Canvas itself never generates such data, but a hand-edited exported page, or content produced by an AI integration like canvas_ai, could contain it. When it did, the component's children were silently reparented to the top level of the tree during hydration, with no error raised to flag the corrupted structure. This fix makes the reserved UUID explicitly forbidden in both positions, so such content is now caught by validation instead of silently misbehaving.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: The Uuid constraint alone let a component instance use the reserved component tree root UUID (a548b48d-58a8-4077-aa04-da9405a6f418) for its uuid or parent_uuid, silently reparenting its children to the top level during hydration with no validation error; ComponentTreeStructureConstraintValidator now rejects it.

Technical details

The fix lives in ComponentTreeStructureConstraintValidator, which validates component tree items for both content entity and config entity component trees. It now checks each item's uuid and parent_uuid against ComponentTreeItemList::ROOT_UUID, using strcasecmp() because the underlying database columns are case-insensitive even though the constraint previously compared case-sensitively. A uuid matching the reserved value raises a violation at the uuid path; a parent_uuid matching it raises a violation at parent_uuid, since placement at the root is expressed by omitting parent_uuid and slot entirely, not by pointing at the root UUID explicitly.

There is no update path: existing data with this violation is not migrated. drush canvas:doctor re-runs these constraints as part of its data health checks, so any pre-existing offending component trees will now surface there. The issue also lists several related gaps left as follow-ups: parent cycles of length two or more still pass validation, duplicate-UUID violations don't name the offending UUID or delta, and config sequence keys aren't bound to each item's uuid.

Upgrade

No code changes are required for callers. Sites with existing component trees should run drush canvas:doctor after upgrading to detect any component instance that illegally used the reserved root UUID (a548b48d-58a8-4077-aa04-da9405a6f418, compared case-insensitively) as its uuid or parent_uuid; such trees will now fail validation and need to be corrected manually since there is no automatic update path.

item.title: #3591839: Prefix-strip redirect misses default-language prefixes and is overridden by ?destination
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591839 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

Canvas's editor could show a blank gray screen on multilingual sites when the site's default language itself has a URL prefix (e.g. /en/ is configured as the prefix for the default English language). The redirect that strips the language prefix from /canvas paths only fired when the current language differed from the default, so a prefixed default-language path reached the React app unstripped and it couldn't route it. Separately, clicking Edit on /admin/content/pages for a page under a prefixed language could bounce the user back to the content overview instead of opening the editor, because the destination query parameter carried by that link survived the redirect and Drupal's core redirect handling used it to override the target. Both problems are fixed: the prefix is now stripped based on what is actually configured for the current URL-negotiated language (default or not), and the query string is preserved on the redirect while destination is cleared from the request so it can no longer hijack the target.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix is in CanvasRouteOptionsEventSubscriber (marked @internal), whose redirect method was renamed from redirectCanvasToDefaultLanguage() to redirectCanvasToUnprefixedPath() to match its new behavior. Instead of comparing the current negotiated language against the site's default language, it now reads the prefix actually configured for the URL-negotiated language from language.negotiation:url.prefixes; an empty prefix means there's nothing to strip, regardless of whether that language is the default. It also checks language.negotiation:url.source against LanguageNegotiationUrl::CONFIG_PATH_PREFIX so a leading path segment is only treated as a language prefix under path-prefix negotiation (not domain negotiation, where a matching segment is a real path component), and it bails out early if the language module isn't installed, since LanguageNegotiationUrl would not be autoloadable in that case.

When a prefix is stripped, the method now builds the LocalRedirectResponse target from $request->getQueryString() so query parameters survive the redirect, and calls $request->query->remove('destination') before building the response so RedirectResponseSubscriber in core cannot later override the computed redirect target with a stale destination value. New kernel tests in CanvasLanguageRoutesTest cover: a default language with its own non-empty prefix, single-language sites with a configured prefix, query-string preservation including destination, a non-matching leading path segment being left untouched, and domain-based negotiation not stripping a path segment that happens to match a configured prefix.

item.title: #3569120: Canvas AI: Expose Props of Blocks to the Agent
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +253/−8 · php +246/−8 · js +6 · txt +1
  • Discussion: #3569120 · 5 contributors · 46 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 5 contributors

Summary

When Canvas AI's page builder agent places a Block component (for example the Site Branding block), it can now see and set that block's actual configuration options instead of just its id and label. Previously the agent only received a block's id, name, and description, so it either produced validation errors when trying to place blocks with required settings, or the values it tried to set (like use_site_logo or use_site_name) were silently dropped and the block was always placed with its default configuration. Now the "Get component context" tool includes each block's available properties (name, description, type, default value, required flag, and allowed choices where applicable), so the agent can configure blocks correctly. Internal-only settings that have no effect on the rendered block (id, provider, admin_label, context_mapping) are still left out.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: Sites with previously saved block descriptions in canvas_ai.component_description.settings have that config automatically rebuilt by canvas_ai_post_update_0007_add_block_props_to_component_description_settings() to include the newly exposed props, while any custom-edited descriptions are preserved.
  • New API: New public CanvasAiPageBuilderHelper::getEnabledBlockComponentsFromStorage() returns enabled block components with prop metadata, loaded directly from storage independent of the current user's access, for use by update hooks and other server-side code.

Technical details

CanvasAiPageBuilderHelper::getAllComponentsKeyedBySource() previously only branched into rich prop extraction for SDC and JS component sources (processSdc(), processCodeComponents()); everything else, including Block components, fell into a generic branch that emitted only id/name/description. A new processBlock() method now builds prop metadata for blocks by reading the block's config schema definition (block.settings.<plugin_id>) via the newly injected TypedConfigManagerInterface, mapping each schema key to a prop with name/description (from the schema label), type, default (preferring the component's saved default_settings over the schema default), a required flag (true unless the schema marks requiredKey === FALSE), and enum values pulled from any Choice constraint. Keys that Canvas can't act on (id, provider, admin_label, context_mapping, the latter because Canvas doesn't apply context mappings at render time) are filtered out via isBlockPropExcluded().

Because the AI update path (drush updb) runs as the anonymous user, and the access-checked component listing returns nothing in that context, a new public getEnabledBlockComponentsFromStorage() method loads enabled block components directly from the Component storage instead. It backs a new canvas_ai_post_update_0007_add_block_props_to_component_description_settings() hook that rebuilds any previously saved canvas_ai.component_description.settings block data with the new prop structure, re-layering each block's previously customized description text on top of the rebuilt data.

Two related bugs surfaced by the missing propSources on blocks were also fixed: AiResponseValidator::validateComponentStructure() dereferenced $clientNormalized['propSources'] unconditionally, which is unset for blocks, now guarded with ?? []; and the UI's removeMediaFields() (used by AiWizard.tsx when placing AI-suggested components) now short-circuits with isPropSourceComponent() since block component definitions have no propSources to filter.

Upgrade

Code integrating with Canvas AI's page builder helper can now fetch block component prop data directly from storage, independent of the current user's permissions:

$blocks = \Drupal::service('canvas_ai.page_builder_helper')
  ->getEnabledBlockComponentsFromStorage();

Sites that previously saved custom block descriptions via the component description settings form will have that config automatically migrated by the canvas_ai_post_update_0007_add_block_props_to_component_description_settings() update hook; no manual action is required.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: January 23, 2026

Key contributors

  • akhil babu (QED42)
  • scott falconer (Acquia)
  • mglaman (Acquia)
  • prabha1997 (QED42)
  • marcus_johansson (FreelyGive)

item.title: #3591785: Strengthen AutoSaveManager to generate stable hashes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591785 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Drupal Canvas's AutoSaveManager hashes each entity's normalized data both to detect when a draft differs from the last saved version and to detect edit conflicts between concurrent editors. Because that normalization step did not consistently cast values to their canonical PHP types before hashing, equivalent data could produce different hashes, making conflict detection and auto-save comparisons unreliable. This issue strengthens the normalization so hashing is stable and deterministic. On update, a database update hook automatically rehashes all existing stored auto-save entries, so no manual action is required, and the previous fallback that treated entries without a stored hash as conflict-free has been removed since it is no longer needed.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: New canvas_post_update_0026_rehash_auto_save_items() update hook rewrites data, data_hash and original_hash for every existing keyvalue-stored Canvas auto-save entry using the strengthened normalization.

Technical details

The root cause was that AutoSaveManager::toStorableArray() stored raw FieldItemListInterface::getValue() output while normalizeEntity() separately cast primitives via PrimitiveInterface::getCastedValue(), and a near-duplicate casting routine existed in ComponentSourceBase. These divergent, partially-raw code paths meant data_hash computation could differ for logically identical data.

Both are replaced by a single new helper, Drupal\canvas\Utility\TypedDataHelper::castRawPhpTypes(), which recursively normalizes any TypedDataInterface: primitives are cast via getCastedValue(), traversable elements are walked to arrays, an absent value stays NULL while a present-but-empty complex value becomes [], and ComponentTreeItem instances are cloned and run through optimizeInputs() first so equivalent component trees always normalize identically. A few properties are special-cased to keep NULL instead of being cast to '' or 0: ComponentTreeItem::NULLABLE_STRING_PROPERTIES (parent_uuid, slot, label), PathItem::langcode, EntityReferenceItem::target_uuid, and TextItemBase::format. AutoSaveManager::toStorableArray() now also uses this helper, and for config entities carrying a component tree it optimizes inputs on a clone before calling toArray().

With hashing now trustworthy for every entry, the special-case fallback in AutoSaveManager that treated auto-save entries lacking original_hash (from before an earlier commit) as having no conflict was removed from detectConflicts(), resolveConflict(), and getAllAutoSaveList(); the AutoSaveEntry phpstan type now declares original_hash and data_hash as always present. canvas.post_update.php adds canvas_post_update_0026_rehash_auto_save_items(), which uses reflection to invoke the now-private normalizeEntity(), generateHash(), and toStorableArray() methods against every stored auto-save keyvalue entry, rebuilding its data, data_hash, and stored-entity hash in place.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3591905: `drush config:import` can fail to update a Component whose `active_version` changed
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591905 · 1 contributor · 5 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

Deploying a Canvas site with drush deploy (or plain drush config:import) could silently fail to update a Component whenever that component's version had changed, for example after adding or removing a prop on a code component. The import would log an error and leave the component at its old version, with no obvious way to tell without checking logs. This particularly affected code components, since the previously known workaround, running a cache rebuild before importing, did not help them: their new configuration only exists in the import itself, so a cache clear just recomputed the old version. This fix makes drush config:import and drush deploy reliably bring Component entities up to date, restoring the expected deploy workflow: edit a component in one environment, export configuration, and import it cleanly in another.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The bug was in how Drupal core's config import updates an existing config entity: ConfigEntityStorage::updateFromStorageRecord() copies every exported property from the sync record, including active_version, onto the already-loaded entity object. But VersionedConfigEntityBase::$loadedVersion is derived, non-exported state that is only set once in the constructor. After the property copy, active_version pointed at the new hash while $loadedVersion still pointed at the old one, and VersionedConfigEntityBase::preSave() throws an EntityStorageException whenever those two disagree. ConfigImporter::importInvokeOwner() catches that exception per-object and just logs it, so the import as a whole appeared to succeed while the Component silently stayed on its old version.

The fix adds a new VersionedConfigEntityStorage (extending ConfigEntityStorage) that overrides updateFromStorageRecord() to call $entity->resetToActiveVersion() after the parent copies the record's properties, re-deriving $loadedVersion from the just-updated active_version. Component now declares this as its storage handler directly. A new VersionedConfigEntityHooks::entityTypeAlter() also assigns VersionedConfigEntityStorage automatically to any entity type implementing VersionedConfigEntityInterface that hasn't already customized its storage class, so other versioned config entity types get the same protection without extra wiring. The invariant that a deliberately loaded historical version cannot be saved (even while syncing) is preserved, since resetToActiveVersion() only runs on the property-copy path triggered by config import, not on manual loadVersion() calls.

item.title: #3591656: Support multi-target-bundle references in code component content-entity-reference props
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591656 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

In Drupal Canvas, code components can declare props that pull data from content entity fields, including fields reached through an entity reference. Until now, if that reference field could point to more than one bundle (for example a "Related content" field that can hold either an Article or a Page), Canvas could not actually render it: the render path threw an explicit error rather than silently producing wrong output, and the Canvas UI's field picker did not let you browse into such a field at all. This issue adds real, end-to-end support: at render time Canvas now resolves the referenced entity first and then picks the correct set of fields for whatever bundle that entity actually turns out to be, and the field picker now lets you browse into a multi-bundle reference field on a per-target-bundle basis. Component authors and site builders no longer need to avoid multi-bundle reference fields when wiring up content-entity-reference props.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

JsComponent::buildReferencePayload() previously threw a \LogicException whenever a reference expression's target was a ReferencedBundleSpecificBranches (the coalesced form produced when a reference field targets multiple bundles, one branch per bundle). It now defers target selection until the referencer resolves to a concrete entity: for each ReferencedBundleSpecificBranches target it calls the new ReferencedBundleSpecificBranches::getBranchForEntityOrNull() to pick the branch matching the resolved entity's entity type and bundle, and for a plain single-bundle target reached through a multi-bundle referencer (an un-coalesced cross-bundle pick) it matches by the target's host entity type and bundle. When nothing matches the resolved entity's bundle, it falls back to a __type-only payload, and cacheability now explicitly includes the traversed entity via addCacheableDependency($entity) since that case has no leaf pick to carry the entity's own cache tags.

On the picker side, ApiUiContentEntityReferenceControllers now offers browsing into a multi-target-bundle reference field, returning one targetBundles entry per bundle. To avoid producing an inexpressible "branch inside a branch" (nested branching, which the string expression format can't yet represent and which the parser rejects), a further multi-bundle descent is withheld once the parent chain already passed through one multi-bundle reference (parentDescendsThroughMultiTargetBundleReference()); that follow-up is tracked in #3591865. The old MultiTargetBundleReferenceNotSupportedConstraint (and its validator) is removed since multi-bundle references are no longer categorically rejected. Two new constraints take its place for the cases still unsupported: EntityFieldExpressionsMustNotNestBranches rejects selections that would coalesce into a nested branch, and EntityFieldExpressionsMustNotMixBundlesInObject rejects picks that read several different fields per bundle across bundles into one object (unrenderable, because each bundle-specific property would throw against the other bundle's entity); mixed-bundle objects becoming a supported branch is tracked in #3591873. A new NestedBranchNotSupportedException lets Coalescer distinguish nested-branch failures from other invalid branch sets, so validation can report the precise "not yet supported" message. The other expression validators (raw-URI, internal-property, multi-valued-field guards) now descend into every branch of a multi-bundle reference instead of skipping it outright, since a violation hidden inside one bundle's branch is still a violation.

item.title: #3582200: component_tree sequence keys sorted lexicographically instead of numerically, breaking component order at 10+ instances per level
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +40/−6 · php +40/−6
  • Discussion: #3582200 · 1 contributor · 3 comments
  • Followers: 2

Summary

Canvas content templates (and other config entities with a component_tree field) could have their component order silently scrambled once a tree contained 10 or more components at the same level, or once a component's position key had multiple ':'-separated segments (e.g. items nested in a slot). This happened whenever Canvas normalized the stored order, such as on save or config import. A tree stored as 0, 1, 2, ..., 9, 10, 11 would come back as 0, 1, 10, 11, 2, 3, ..., and this corrupted order then propagated to the Canvas layout API and to preview rendering. This fix ensures component order is preserved correctly regardless of how many components a level or slot contains.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause was that Canvas encodes a component tree's structure into string keys, such as 4, 4:the_body:0, or 4:the_body:0:<uuid>, and then relies on sorting those keys to recover the intended order. Three call sites, ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::preSave(), and ComponentTreeConfigEntityTransformer::import() and its internal computeExportSequenceKeys(), used PHP's ksort(), which compares keys as plain strings. That makes 10 sort before 2, since lexicographic comparison looks at the first character first.

The fix replaces all three ksort() calls with uksort($tree, \strnatcmp(...)), using PHP's natural-order string comparison so that whole-number segments within the ':'-delimited keys are compared numerically (9 before 10) while still keeping parent keys (4) ordered before their child keys (4:the_body:0). ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::preSave() additionally gained a new componentTreeSequenceIsPositionEncoded() helper, which checks whether the tree's keys are still position-encoded (not yet re-keyed by UUID) so the natural sort is applied only when needed, covering the config install/update path that bypasses the sync import transformer.

item.title: #3591820: Publishing a symmetrically-translated canvas_page 422s when a default-language edit changes a non-translatable component input
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591820 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Sites that translate canvas_page entities with content_translation could hit an HTTP 422 error when trying to publish a page after editing a non-translatable ("symmetric") component input, such as an image's width, a section's padding_bottom, or a heading's element (h1 to h6) tag, on a component instance that also exists in another language's translation. The publish would be rejected even though saving the same change directly would have succeeded. This is now fixed: publishing converges the non-default translation's copy of the changed input to match the default translation, and the publish succeeds as expected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause was an ordering mismatch between validation and synchronization. content_translation's presave hook is what converges "symmetric" (non-translatable) field columns across a translated entity's translations, but that convergence only happens inside EntityInterface::save(). Canvas's publish path, ApiAutoSaveController::getConflictAwareContentEntityViolations(), validates the entity with $entity->validate() before save() runs, so ComponentTreeSymmetricalTranslationConstraint saw the pre-sync, stale, intermediate state (the auto-save snapshot only ever carries the edited default-language translation) and rejected it.

The fix introduces SymmetricalTranslationSynchronizationTrait, used by both ClientDataToEntityConverter and ApiAutoSaveController. It wraps content_translation.synchronizer (injected as an optional $translationSynchronizer constructor argument, since content_translation is an optional dependency) and exposes synchronizeTranslations()/canSynchronizeTranslations(). getConflictAwareContentEntityViolations() now validates a cloned copy of the entity with translations synchronized, while leaving the entity that is actually saved untouched, so content_translation's presave hook remains the single synchronization pass. This distinction matters because FieldTranslationSynchronizer::synchronizeItems() is not idempotent after a structural edit (an insert or reorder): running it twice on an already-synchronized entity maps inputs to the wrong deltas and corrupts translations. ClientDataToEntityConverter::convert() similarly synchronizes in place before validating, but only on auto-save (never before an actual save()), and only when the entity in hand is the default translation, since a non-default translation being edited is itself a synchronization target and must not be silently overwritten before its own violation can be reported.</technical> <parameter name="collaboration">

item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591716 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

In the Canvas experience builder, editing a component with boolean properties (for example a "card-program" component) could cause all of its boolean toggle switches to visually flip to ON as soon as any other, unrelated prop was changed, even though the user never touched the toggle. This was purely a display and initial-state bug: it could mislead editors into thinking a boolean prop was enabled when it was not. [] fix was applied to the source field.

item.title: #3573022: [upstream] Data loss: `drush config:import` deletes config (e.g. code component + component config entities) and bypasses config system data integrity checks
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3573022 · 3 contributors · 18 comments
  • Followers: 4
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

Running drush config:import could silently delete in-use Canvas code components without triggering Canvas's built-in safety mechanisms, leaving dangling references in page content and producing a white screen of death (WSOD) on every page that referenced those components. There was no way to recover without directly editing the database. Canvas now blocks any config import that would delete a component still in use on a page, giving site owners a clear error message and keeping the site intact. Unused components can still be removed via config import.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause is in Drupal core's ConfigImporter::importConfig(), which uses the low-level Config::delete() to remove configuration entries rather than calling ConfigEntityBase::delete(). That bypass means ConfigEntityBase::preDelete() is never invoked, and therefore Component::onDependencyRemoval() never runs. That method is what Canvas relies on to switch an in-use component to its fallback source; without it, deleting a canvas.js_component.* or canvas.component.js.* config entity via drush config:import leaves live page content pointing at configuration that no longer exists.

The fix adds ComponentConfigImportValidator, a final class extending ConfigImportValidateEventSubscriberBase, registered as a service in canvas.services.yml. During ConfigEvents::IMPORT_VALIDATE it inspects the deletion list for two danger vectors: (A) a Component config entity is itself scheduled for deletion, and (B) non-component configuration that a retained Component depends on is being deleted (detected via ConfigManagerInterface::findConfigEntityDependenciesAsEntities()). For every endangered Component the subscriber calls ComponentAudit::hasUsages() for both published revisions and auto-save drafts; if either returns true, the import is aborted via ConfigImporter::logError() with an explanatory message naming the affected component.

This is explicitly a stopgap until core is fixed. The class docblock references two upstream issues: one to route config-import deletions through onDependencyRemoval() and one (#2414951) that would add this class of detection to core itself, at which point the subscriber could be removed rather than just adjusted.

item.title: #3591667: Add `canvas:doctor` Drupal CLI command to check health of Canvas' data: validate every Canvas (content|config) entity + translation, validate every non-Canvas content entity component tree field revision+translation, and more
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591667 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The Canvas module now ships a canvas:doctor command (requiring Drupal 11.4's dr CLI) that validates all Canvas data and reports integrity problems. It runs nine distinct health checks: four system checks (Canvas update paths executed, config entities that escaped the update path, whether all installed extensions are at tagged releases, and whether every component source plugin supports schema evolution) and five data checks (Canvas config entities, default content revisions, past revisions, forward/draft revisions, and auto-save snapshots). Each check reports a count of healthy vs. failing items, a duration, and optional per-violation details with a prescription for remediation. The command can output a human-readable table or structured JSON. Validation also runs incrementally via cron on sites that never use the CLI, so health records stay warm without requiring manual intervention.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: New canvas_health_records table is created lazily on first write; no update hook is required.
  • New API: New canvas:doctor CLI command (requires Drupal 11.4+) with --checks, --all-checks, --no-cache, --details, and --format=json options for auditing Canvas data integrity.

Technical details

The implementation is organized into five @internal classes under src/Health/ plus the command itself in src/Command/DoctorCommand.php.

HealthCheck is a string-backed PHP enum with nine cases split into system checks (run once per invocation, never cached) and data checks (streamed as generators, results persisted). The isSystemCheck() and findingsAreRisks() methods are the single source of truth for those splits: adding a new case without updating both exhaustive match expressions causes a PHPStan failure.

Doctor is the validation engine. runDataChecks() yields CheckItem structs via generators, which lets DoctorCommand display a live progress bar without loading all entities into memory first. runCronWindow() accepts an offset and limit, enabling HealthHooks::cron() to advance a cursor stored in Drupal state across separate cron runs. Each data check's freshness signal is computed at the moment Doctor visits the item, not when Inventory listed it, so paginated results from a previous cron run do not carry stale freshness data.

HealthRecords persists results in the canvas_health_records database table (keyed on data_key + check). The table is created lazily on first write rather than via a formal install hook. Freshness is determined by matching two fingerprints: an environment fingerprint (Canvas schema version, count of applied and pending post-updates, xxh64 hash of all installed extension versions) computed by Environment, and a data fingerprint per item (cache-tag checksum for config and content entities, a precomputed data hash for auto-save snapshots). If any installed extension reports no release version (dev), HealthRecords::isFresh() unconditionally returns false, disabling all result reuse.

UpdatesEscapedConfig detection uses reflection to enumerate CanvasConfigUpdater::needs*() methods, filters to those whose first required parameter type-matches the entity being inspected, and calls each. Deprecation emissions from those methods are suppressed during the audit by temporarily calling setDeprecationsEnabled(FALSE). The DoctorCommand itself is thin: it delegates all logic to Doctor so the same validation can power the planned web UI (#3588907 via Drupal Batch API).
